arcs.title: THE TRUE MERCHANT TEST
arcs.summary: Akbar asks Birbal to find the true merchant in the kingdom. Birbal announces a test, and merchants from across the land arrive claiming they have Akbar's desired items.

arcs.title: THE POOR OLD MAN'S CLAIM
arcs.summary: A poor old man arrives at court with nothing but time to sell. The other merchants mock him, but Birbal sees the wisdom in his claim of selling time as a valuable gift.

arcs.title: THE TRUE FRIEND TEST
arcs.summary: Akbar asks Birbal about true friendship. A poor friend offers all he has to help Akbar, showing selflessness and loyalty despite his own lack of wealth.

arcs.title: THE STOLEN COW CASE
arcs.summary: A farmer complains that his cow was stolen. Birbal announces a reward for returning the lost cow. The real thief, fearing exposure, returns it but demands half the reward.

arcs.title: THE INTRUDER POET
arcs.summary: Akbar is troubled by a dream of an intruder in his palace. Birbal advises treating the intruder kindly and offering him food, which turns out to be a drunk poet.

arcs.title: BIRBAL'S FIRST MEETING
arcs.summary: 6. BIRBAL'S FIRST MEETING: Akbar meets Mahesh Das (future Birbal) in the forest. He helps Akbar find his way and is rewarded with a royal ring, which he later recognizes as valuable when he grows up.

arcs.title: THE FOOLS LIST
arcs.summary: Akbar challenges Birbal to list six fools in one month. Birbal identifies foolishness in others but admits that even he and Akbar are part of the group, showing wisdom through humility.

arcs.title: BIRBAL'S GURU
arcs.summary: Akbar wants to meet Birbal's guru. Birbal arranges a meeting with a woodcutter whom he elevates as his guru. The monk remains silent and indifferent to gold, impressing Akbar.

arcs.title: THE THREE QUESTIONS
arcs.summary: Akbar asks Birbal three questions about God. Birbal's son answers using everyday examples like sugar dissolving in milk or butter coming from curd to explain divine principles.

arcs.title: THE MAGIC DONKEY
arcs.summary: The queen loses a necklace and other items. Birbal uses a magical donkey with a special scent on its tail to identify the thief, who avoids touching it out of fear.

arcs.title: BIRBAL'S CHILDREN
arcs.summary: Birbal is late for court because his children are stubborn. Akbar doubts him, but Birbal proves how difficult parenting is by acting like a child and refusing to eat sugarcane until he gets what he wants.

arcs.title: THE KHICHDI CHALLENGE
arcs.summary: Akbar challenges Birbal to prove someone can survive the cold night in the Yamuna River. Birbal uses a poor man's cleverness and then plays a trick with khichdi cooked far from fire, teaching Akbar not to dismiss others' efforts.

arcs.title: THE CROW COUNT CHALLENGE
arcs.summary: Akbar asks how many crows are in the kingdom. Birbal cleverly replies that if there are more than he said, they're visiting relatives; fewer means some have gone elsewhere, impressing Akbar with his wit.

arcs.title: THE HONEST THIEF
arcs.summary: Akbar wants to find a thief. Birbal gives each suspect an equal-length stick and claims the guilty one will cut it shorter out of fear. The thief does so, revealing himself.

arcs.title: THE RICH MERCHANT'S DILEMMA
arcs.summary: 15. THE HONEST THIEF: Akbar wants to find a thief. Birbal gives each suspect an equal-length stick and claims the guilty one will cut it shorter out of fear. The thief does so, revealing himself.

arcs.title: THE WASHERMAN'S DONKEY
arcs.summary: A dispute arises over a donkey between a washerman and a nobleman. Birbal dresses the donkey in fancy clothes and brings it to court, exposing the nobleman's mistake.

episodes.title: Test of True Merchant
beats: Akbar asks Birbal to find the true merchant in the kingdom.
Birbal announces a test to identify the true merchant.
Merchants from across the land arrive at court claiming they have the desired item.
Some merchants bring silk cloth, others bring jewels and gems.
episodes.hook: Birbal rejects all the merchants, leaving everyone confused and wondering who will pass his test.

episodes.title: Time is a Merchant
beats: A poor old man arrives at court with nothing but time to sell.
The other merchants mock the old man for trying to sell time.
Birbal listens carefully to the old man's claim about selling time as a valuable gift.
Birbal praises the old man's wisdom and insight into the true value of time.
episodes.hook: Birbal praises the old man's wisdom, leaving Akbar curious about the true value of time.

episodes.title: Friendship Tested
beats: Akbar asks Birbal about the nature of true friendship.
A poor friend, despite having little, offers all he has to assist Akbar.
The poor friend sacrifices his own needs to support Akbar's request.
episodes.hook: Akbar is left speechless as the poor friend gives up everything for his trust.

episodes.title: The Soul of a Friend
beats: Akbar is moved by the selflessness and loyalty of the poor friend.
Birbal explains that true friendship is shown through sacrifice and unwavering support.
The poor friend's actions demonstrate deep loyalty despite his own lack of wealth.
episodes.hook: Birbal's words echo in Akbar's heart as he realizes true friendship is not measured by wealth.

episodes.title: THE TRUE FRIEND TEST 3
beats: Akbar concludes that true friends are those who help even when they have nothing to give.
The story highlights the value of selflessness and trust in friendships.
Akbar learns that true friendship is not about wealth but about character.
The arc ends with Akbar recognizing the importance of loyalty over material gain.
episodes.hook: Akbar stands in silence, eyes glistening, as he declares the poor friend his truest companion.
